sentences.text: It is the case of applicant that he is the manufacturer of Kamdhenu Suddh Ghee, whereas respondent No.2 is neither the dealer nor the retailer of applicant.

On 17.03.2011 respondent No.1 i.e. Food Inspector alongwith other officers inspected the business enterprise of respondent No.2 and took sample of various food items including Kamdhenu Shuddu Ghee packet of 500 gms by purchasing three packets of said 500 gms Kamdhenu Shuddh Ghee from respondent No.2 against payment of Rs.369/-.
Kamdhenu Shuddh Ghee was sent for analysis to Food Laboratory.

Public Analyst submitted its report dated 11.04.2011 and the said sample of Kamdhenu Shuddh Ghee was found adulterated and in pursuance thereof respondent No.1 obtained due sanction for prosecution of respondent No.2 as per Section 20(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and preferred the complaint/charge sheet.

Charges against respondent No.2 were duly framed and during trial Food Inspector namely Shri Arunesh Kumar Patel was examined as P.W.-1, whereas other two witnesses of prosecution namely Shri Kishan Chand Masani and Dr. Pankaj Shukla were examined as P.W.-2 and P.W.-3 respectively.
All the three witnesses did not allege anything against the applicant.
Respondent No.2 also furnished his statement in defence as D.W.-1.
He also did not allege anything against the applicant.
The final arguments of the case were heard on 13.07.2018 and the matter was fixed for final judgment on 26.07.2018.
On 26.07.2018 the final judgment was not delivered as respondent No.2 was not present and the matter was again posted for delivery of judgment on 03.08.2018.

On 03.08.2018 respondent No.2 preferred an application under Section 20-A of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act to implead the applicant as co-accused for being the manufacturer of the said Kamdhenu Shuddh Ghee.
Although notice of said application was issued to applicant but the same was not received and therefore, he could not appear before the Trial Court.

Trial Court pronounced the final judgment on 18.12.2018 and acquitted respondent No.2 on account of breach and violation of provisions of Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act as copy of the report of Public Analyst was supplied to respondent No.2 on 15.11.2011 whereas shelf life of sample was only till November, 2011.
Trial Court also granted liberty to respondent No.1 to destroy the sample under section 18 of Food Adulteration Act.

However, in the meanwhile, Trial Court issued warrant of arrest against the applicant and by impugned order dated 07.05.2019 Trial Court has framed charges under Section 7(i) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) of Food Adulteration Act against the applicant.
3. Challenging the order passed by Court below, it is submitted by counsel for applicant that applicant has been implicated only in the year 2018 whereas samples were collected on 17.03.2011.

It is further submitted that by framing charge against applicant in the year 2019 the valuable right of applicant to get the sample retested by the Central Laboratory has been violated and therefore,
prosecution of applicant is bad.

Furthermore, only in case if any receipt is issued by manufacturer in favour of retailer, then it can be said that manufacturer has indemnified the retailer as provided under Section 14 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
However, no such receipt was ever produced by retailer, therefore, it cannot be said that applicant had ever indemnified the retailer.
4. Per contra, counsel for respondent no.2 has supported the findings recorded by Court below.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for parties.

6. Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 reads as under:
"13. Report of public analyst.-(1) xxxx xxxx (2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated,
the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any,
whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A,
forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory."
7.

From plain reading of Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, it is clear that if a person is aggrieved by the report submitted by analyst then he has a right to file an application for re-testing by Central laboratory.

8. In the present case, the report of analyst is dated 11/04/2011, whereas applicant has been impleaded as an additional accused in the year 2018 and charges have been framed by order dated 07/05/2019.

Not only the shelf life of Ghee had already expired, but subsequent impleadment of applicant as an additional accused is in violation of Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act as his valuable right to apply for re-testing from Central laboratory would stand violated.

9. Furthermore, Section 14 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act reads as under:-
"14. Manufacturers, distributors and dealers to give warranty.-No manufacturer or distributor of, or dealer in any article of food shall sell such article to any vendor unless he also gives a warranty in writing in the prescribed form about the nature and quality of such article to the vendor:
Provided that a bill, cash memorandum or invoice in respect of the sale of any article of food given by a manufacturer or distributor of, or dealer in, such article to the vendor thereof shall be deemed to be a warranty given by such manufacturer,
distributor or dealer under this section.
Explanation.-In this section, in sub-section (2) of section 19 and in section 20A, the expression "distributor" shall include a commission agent."
10.
Thus, it is clear that only if any receipt is issued by manufacturer in favour of the retailer, then it can be said that manufacturer had indemnified the retailer.

3 11.

sentences.text: Admittedly, respondent No.2 had not filed any receipt to show that the applicant had indemnified him.
If any adulteration takes place after the goods are supplied, then the manufacturer cannot be held responsible in absence of receipt for the purchase of the said good by the retailer.

12. Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of considered opinion that Trial Court committed an error by summoning the applicant as an additional accused as well as by framing charge by order dated 07/05/2019.
13. Accordingly, order dated 07/05/2019 passed by Special Magistrate (Food Adulteration and Prevention Act, Bhopal in Criminal Case No.8439/2011 is hereby set aside.

entities.text: Special Magistrate (Food Adulteration and Prevention Act, Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Applicant is hereby discharged.
14. Application succeeds and is hereby allowed.
